proposal.title: Sync-revealed Hedge gating between SNI-style damped trend prediction and last-observed hold for stale remote GNN embeddings: an application test
proposal.hypothesis: On a fixed single-process partition emulation of small node-classification graphs, a per-partition-pair two-expert Hedge gate updated only at actual sync epochs reduces the mean relative stale-embedding error, ||x_used - h_true|| / ||h_true||, over stale epochs by at least 5% versus the best of three controls: hold, ungated predictor, and a development-tuned fixed mixture. The prediction and sync budgets are identical across arms.
proposal.baseline: The SNI-GNN Algorithm 2 self-feeding damped trend predictor, x_pred = x_last + v·Δ·e^{-βΔ}, applied to boundary nodes selected by sampling. The comparison also includes last-observed hold, which SNI uses for unsampled nodes. The implementation reference is sni-method chunks 0004–0005. No SNI code is supplied, so this is a reimplementation from the text and its fidelity is a baseline-coverage gap. SAT (a learned online predictor) is a stronger competitor, but only its abstract is available. It is listed as an uncovered baseline.
proposal.operator_delta: Replace the fixed choice between predictor and hold with a convex combination for each node group g. The combination is x_used = w_g·x_pred + (1 - w_g)·x_last. The weight w_g comes from exponentially weighted (Hedge) updates. These updates use losses that become available only when a sync reveals true embeddings and are scored against the predictions frozen during the preceding interval.

contribution_claims.text: An application question: whether sync-revealed expert gating between damped trend prediction and hold reduces harmful extrapolation in stale GNN embeddings.
A frozen-prediction, sync-revealed loss protocol with horizon-matched loss attribution. Losses are computed for every stale offset Δ by storing frozen outputs.
Expected result (hypothesis only): the gate beats the best fixed operator only when the predictor's relative quality changes over training, for example after the prespecified learning-rate drop.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: Source premises: embeddings 'evolve smoothly', SNI uses a fixed sync interval s, and the error theorem assumes a bounded second difference with an undamped Taylor predictor. Theorem IV.1 does not cover the damped, EMA-baselined, self-fed implementation, so no guarantee is claimed. Target assumptions (inferred): there is non-stationarity in which operator is better, and losses can be logged at revealed syncs. Regimes without such shifts are outside the hypothesis's scope; they are not contradictions of it.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: For each group g, keep a weight w_g. Steps: (1) At sync time t0, freeze w_g for the interval. (2) For each stale epoch t0+Δ with Δ = 1..s-1, compute x_pred(Δ) and x_last. Use x_used = w_g·x_pred + (1-w_g)·x_last and store x_pred(Δ) per node; storing per-node scalars is not enough because predictor state must be matched. (3) At the next sync t1 = t0+s, h(t1) is observed. Compute L_P = mean_i ||x_pred_i(s) - h_i(t1)||² / ||h_i(t1)||², and L_H the same way for x_last. Only the end horizon Δ = s is revealed; intermediate h is never shown to the gate. (4) Update w_g ∝ w_g·e^{-η·L_P} and (1-w_g) ∝ (1-w_g)·e^{-η·L_H}, with a fixed-share floor ε = 0.01. (5) Feed the predictor its observation exactly as in Algorithm 2.
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: This reduces exactly to Hedge or Fixed Share with delayed feedback over two experts (arXiv 1902.10433). No new learning algorithm survives simplification. The remaining effect is empirical: whether the losses at Δ = s rank the experts correctly for shorter Δ. Damping e^{-βΔ} makes the predictor's error depend on Δ, so this ranking is unresolved. Costs are 1 scalar per group plus a buffer of s·|sampled|·d for frozen predictions, or reuse of x_pred at Δ = s only, which adds O(|sampled|·d) memory.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: A global fixed mixture w* tuned on the development graph, with zero runtime state and no adaptivity. It also covers the better fixed operator (w = 0 or 1).
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Cheap screening on synchronous trajectories. Record full-sync trajectories, then emulate stale epochs offline. Compare the Hedge gate against w* and the best fixed operator on stale-epoch relative error, using both the ordinary schedule and an LR×0.1 drop at 50% of epochs. If Hedge does not beat w* by 5%, stop before closed-loop training.

evidence.supports: Exact form of the baseline predictor.
Hold is an existing operator inside SNI.
Feedback arrives only at fixed syncs.
The gate is an existing expert rule.

assumptions: The ranking of predictor versus hold at Δ = s agrees with the ranking at Δ < s in at least 80% of intervals; this is checked offline using full trajectories.
The relative merit of the two operators shifts after the LR change.
Group-level gating at the partition-pair level is sufficient.

data_paths.operation: Score frozen x_pred(s) and x_last, then apply the Hedge update
data_paths.possible_leakage: Intermediate-epoch truth is used only in offline evaluation and never by the gate. The w* tuned on dev must not see test graphs or seeds.

proposal.counterexample: A smooth, monotone trajectory in which the predictor is always better. Then w → 1 and the gate only adds lag relative to the ungated predictor, so it matches or underperforms the better fixed operator.
proposal.matched_control: The same predictor state, the same sampled nodes, s, and feedback logging, with w fixed at the dev-tuned w*, at 0, or at 1. A random-weight-sequence control is also included.

experiment.development: Cora and CiteSeer with public splits, 4 METIS-like partitions emulated in one process on CPU/MPS, a 2-layer GCN, s = 4, seeds 0–2. The protocol is frozen, η is tuned on a grid of 3 values, and w* is tuned here.
experiment.heldout: Amazon-Photo and Coauthor-CS with fixed random splits, seeds 10–14, never inspected before the protocol is frozen. The gate must pass trajectory screening first. Closed-loop training is then run with the ordinary schedule and the LR drop.
experiment.metric: Primary: mean relative stale-embedding error over stale epochs, averaged across seeds. Closed-loop: final test accuracy as mean ± std. No hardware speedup claims are made.
experiment.kill_threshold: Reject if the error reduction relative to min(w*, hold, predictor) is below 5% on held-out data, or if closed-loop accuracy gains are within 1 std or below 0.3 points in either schedule.

proposal.prior_art_difference: The gate overlaps entirely with delayed-feedback Hedge and Fixed Share. SNI selects between prediction and hold statically by node importance. SAT learns a predictor online; whether it gates between operators cannot be verified from the abstract. There is no matching local experiment. The only unverified difference is applying a sync-revealed two-expert rule to SNI-style operators, not a new algorithm.

evidence.supports: SNI already uses both operators, prediction and hold, but chooses between them statically by node importance.
The gating rule itself is existing delayed-feedback expert weighting.
Adaptive staleness reduction exists in SAT, but its mechanism is visible only at abstract level.

claim_assessments.reason: Both operators and the expert rule appear in the examined evidence. None of the examined chunks applies a sync-revealed loss-driven gate between SNI's predictor and hold. SAT's internals are unknown from its abstract alone. This absence does not establish novelty.

evidence.supports: Scoring experts on losses revealed after a delay is generic delayed-feedback Hedge.

claim_assessments.reason: Delayed scoring is covered by the Hedge evidence. The horizon-matched attribution part is not found in the evidence. It is also internally inconsistent: C2 says losses are computed for every stale offset Δ, but the proposal's own mechanism says only Δ = s is revealed and intermediate truth is never shown to the gate. Per-Δ losses cannot be computed online, because h(t0+Δ) for Δ < s is never observed.
This is an expected result, a hypothesis rather than an observation. No supplied evidence reports how predictor-versus-hold ranking behaves across a learning-rate drop.

mechanism_check.assumption_scope: Source assumptions: SNI assumes smooth evolution and a fixed s. Theorem IV.1 assumes a bounded second difference with an undamped Taylor predictor, so it does not cover Algorithm 2's damped, self-fed form. Target assumptions: which operator is better changes over training, and the loss at Δ = s ranks the experts correctly at Δ < s. Stationary regimes are excluded from the hypothesis's scope; they do not contradict it.
mechanism_check.specialized_operation: Algorithm 2 steps (d) and (i) self-feed x_pred into x_last and set t_last = t. If Predict is called every stale epoch, then Δ = 1 at each call, and 'x_last' during stale epochs is the previous prediction, not the last observed value. Hold must therefore be a separate cached value, h_sync(t0). The gate then computes x_used = w·x_pred + (1 - w)·h_sync. At t1 it scores L_P = rel-err(x_pred at t1 before the observation is written) and L_H = rel-err(h_sync(t0)), then sets w ∝ w·e^{-ηL_P} with Fixed Share. The predictor state must be fed x_pred, not x_used, so that the gate does not alter the expert.
mechanism_check.remaining_effect: The gate is an algorithmic no-op relative to delayed Fixed Share. What survives is only the empirical question of whether per-group adaptive w beats a tuned constant w* on non-stationary trajectories. Also unresolved: the operator definitions under self-feeding, which determine whether 'hold' even differs from the predictor's internal state.
mechanism_check.simplest_baseline: A dev-tuned constant w*, with w = 0 and w = 1 as special cases. It needs no runtime state but cannot track shifts. A second baseline is SNI's static importance-based selection.
mechanism_check.distinguishing_test: Run offline replay on full-sync trajectories with an explicitly separate h_sync. Compute per-interval regret of Hedge versus w*, before and after the learning-rate drop. Check whether the ranking at Δ = s agrees with the ranking at Δ < s in at least 80% of intervals.

review.reason: The gate reduces to known delayed Hedge, so any value is empirical. The proposal has two problems to fix. First, it conflates Algorithm 2's self-fed x_last with last-observed hold; it must define hold as the sync-time value and keep the predictor's input independent of the gate. Second, C2's per-Δ loss claim contradicts the stated information path. Any benefit also hinges on the untested assumption that end-of-interval ranking transfers to shorter horizons. In closed loop, the arms change h_true itself, so error comparisons must come from offline replay.

evidence.supports: Algorithm 2 writes predictions into the state used as x_last.
x_last and Δ are reset at each call, so hold must be defined separately.

review.strongest_counterargument: The proposal itself admits there is no algorithmic novelty and specifies a cheap offline kill test. The definitional issue is easy to fix, so a direct 'test' decision would be reasonable.
review.required_test: Run the offline replay on Cora with a separate h_sync and the predictor fed only x_pred. Compare Hedge against w* and the best fixed operator under both schedules. Also measure the rate of ranking agreement between Δ = s and Δ < s. Stop if the Hedge reduction is below 5%.
